subject: SLA clarification: uptime floor, batched latency carveouts, and monthly credit escrow
messages:
From: Elena Morales <em@skyline-analytics.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Skyline Procurement <procurement@skyline-analytics.com>, Skyline Legal <legal@skyline-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA questions on uptime %, latency carveouts, and monthly credits

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's routing and caching story. Procurement and Legal asked me to follow up on a few SLA items before we move to contracting: 

- Standard uptime: Skyline's infosec would like 99.95% for hosted API endpoints, but their product team is worried about batched analytics endpoints where latency spikes under heavy aggregation. They asked whether batched endpoints could have a different latency SLO or explicit carveout.
- Maintenance windows: The redlined SLA from Legal proposes a 6-hour monthly maintenance window exclusion and a separate monthly credit cap tied to severity. Your standard template shows 4 hours. Can we align on what maintenance carveouts we can offer for enterprise accounts?
- Credit calculation: Procurement wants clarity on how monthly service credits are calculated (per-incident vs aggregated monthly shortfall) and whether credits can be held in escrow or applied to future invoices.

I've attached our redlines — can you review and propose language that addresses our concerns while staying close to Redwood's standard? We'd like to keep this short so procurement can approve the PO next week.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Cloud Partnerships
Skyline Analytics

Attachment: redlined-sla-draft-v3.pdf

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <em@skyline-analytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA questions on uptime %, latency carveouts, and monthly credits

Elena —

Appreciate the clear summary and the redlines. Looping in Ben (legal) and Aditya (reliability/product) to help draft precise language. Quick responses to your bullets: 

- Standard uptime: We are willing to commit to 99.95% for the hosted API for the agreed scope of routed text/generation endpoints. For Skyline's batched analytics endpoints we can propose a separate SLO bucket: 99.9% uptime with a latency SLO expressed as P95 <= 1.2s for single-token streams and P95 <= 2.8s for batched aggregation calls (these numbers reflect observed production profiles for batched workloads). Let us know if the product team needs different percentiles.

- Maintenance windows: We can expand the maintenance carveout to 6 hours monthly for dedicated enterprise accounts, provided we also include a notice window (72 hours for planned maintenance >1 hour) and a monthly cap on planned maintenance of 12 hours (two of the six-hour windows can be used as emergency maintenance if mutually agreed).

- Credit calculation & escrow: We typically calculate credits on an aggregated monthly shortfall basis (total minutes below the uptime floor across the month, mapped to a credit percentage of that month's invoice). We can offer credits applied to future invoices or, upon request, deposit a notional credit into an escrow account for multi-year deals (requires finance/legal coordination).

Ben — can you suggest specific contractual language for the 99.9 vs 99.95 split and the escrow option? Aditya — can you confirm the latency carveout numbers are achievable for Skyline's expected burst profile (you saw their telemetry in the trial?). Monica — FYI for billing implications.

Next step: I'll circulate a redline that maps Skyine's requested changes to our standard template. If Skyline is OK with the dual-bucket approach (hosted gen endpoints 99.95 / batched analytics 99.9 with defined latency P95s), that should unblock procurement.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Elena Morales <em@skyline-analytics.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, Skyline Legal <legal@skyline-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA questions on uptime %, latency carveouts, and monthly credits

Elena / team —

I've reviewed the redlines and Marissa's proposal. Below is suggested contract language we can insert into Section 3 (Service Levels) and Section 7 (Remedies):

--- Suggested insertion (plain language first, then legal lingo):
1) Service Buckets: The Parties agree that Customer's endpoints are categorized as (a) "Interactive Generation" endpoints (applies to single-request text and chat APIs) and (b) "Batched Analytics" endpoints (applies to multi-record aggregation/embedding/batch inference calls). Redwood shall provide the following availability commitments: 99.95% monthly availability for Interactive Generation; 99.9% monthly availability for Batched Analytics.

2) Latency SLO for Batched Analytics: For Batched Analytics endpoints, Redwood warrants a latency SLO of P95 <= 2.8 seconds and P99 <= 6.0 seconds measured on successful request completions, excluding cached prefix hits. Excluded from the latency calculation are scheduled maintenance windows and force-majeure events.

3) Maintenance Carveout: Customer agrees to a scheduled maintenance carveout not to exceed 6 hours per calendar month. Redwood will provide at least seventy-two (72) hours' advance notice for planned maintenance longer than one (1) hour. Planned maintenance in excess of the monthly carveout requires Customer consent and will not count toward availability calculations.

4) Credit Calculation: Service credits will be calculated on an aggregated monthly basis as follows: For each Service Bucket, total downtime minutes below the applicable uptime threshold will be converted to a credit percentage of the monthly invoice using the attached monthly-credit-calculator.xlsx mapping table. Credits are applied to the next invoice unless the Parties agree to place the credit in escrow for later use; escrowed credits will be documented in a separate Schedule and are only redeemable against Redwood charges.

5) Credit Cap and Severity: Monthly credit cap remains at 50% of the monthly invoice for all combined credits. Individual incident credits will follow the severity ladder in Section 7.2.

---

I attached the legal redline with these clauses inserted. On escrow: we can support the escrow concept for multi-year committed seats but will need Skyline's finance to sign off on the escrow instrument (we prefer a ledger entry applied to future invoices rather than a third-party escrow trustee to keep operations simple).

Aditya — can you confirm our telemetry windowing approach (P95/P99 measurement rules) aligns with how Skyline's trial data was collected, and whether we should narrow the exclusion clause about "cached prefix hits"?

If Skyline agrees to the mixed-bucket availability, we can remove the contentious 99.95-only ask from their redline and proceed to DocuSign.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Contracts & Pricing
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redlined-sla-draft-v3-ben-redline.pdf; monthly-credit-calculator.xlsx

From: Elena Morales <em@skyline-analytics.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Skyline Procurement <procurement@skyline-analytics.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA questions on uptime %, latency carveouts, and monthly credits

Marissa / Ben / Aditya —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and for translating our asks into concrete language — very helpful. A few quick confirmations from our side after internal review: 

- The dual-bucket approach (99.95% interactive / 99.9% batched) is acceptable to the product team provided the P95/P99 latency SLOs are included as you suggested.
- Maintenance carveout at 6 hours with 72-hour notice is fine; procurement will keep the option to require consent for additional planned maintenance.
- Escrow: Procurement prefers a ledger-style escrow (credit applied against future invoices) rather than a third-party account. They'll sign the separate schedule if you provide the standard escrow schedule.

Next steps: We'll share a clean copy of your redline with one small tweak (adding a dashboard dashboard metric name for the P95/P99 measurements so our observability team has a single source of truth). If you can send the final redline + DocuSign link for the master SaaS agreement and the escrow schedule, we'll aim to return countersigned by end of next week.

Appreciate everyone's help — this gets us over the line for the PO.

Best,
Elena
Head of Cloud Partnerships
Skyline Analytics
